Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The players have made their way out in the middle. Craig Ervine and Joylord Gumbie are the openers for Zimbabwe. Karan KC comes to bowl. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Zimbabwe struggled with the ball at the start and it was Wellington Masakadza who provided them the crucial breakthroughs of both Nepal's openers. Richard Ngarava chipped in with four wickets on his name whilst Tendai Chatara and Blessing Muzarabani had one in their bank.

Right then, Nepal has posted a total of 290 runs on the board and will be hoping for their bowlers to defend this. For Zimbabwe, the onus is now on their batters to put up a good stand and chase this down. Which side will get over the line in this inaugural game? To find out, do join us for the second essay in a short while.

It was a great display of batting from Nepal's side. Their openers gave them a perfect start with Kushal Bhurtel playing as an aggressor and Aasif Sheikh, who played as a second fiddle. The opening partnership was broken after 171 runs when Kushal Bhurtel fell for a yorker and was dismissed for a heartbreaking 99 runs. Nonetheless, he made sure the job was well done. Let me remind you that Bhurtel was dropped twice, first in the fourth over and next in the 27th over. Kushal Malla and Rohit Paudel played well in the middle order scoring 41 and 31 respectively which made Nepal reach a good total of 290 runs.
After a sensational opening partnership by Nepal, a brilliant spell from Richard Ngarava at the backend keeps the total below 300 for Zimbabwe.

TOSS - Zimbabwe has won the toss and they have elected to BOWL first.

On the flip side, Nepal will need to adapt to the circumstances and perform well against Zimbabwe. In this initial match, the team needs to maintain composure in all areas and bring their A-game. Can they do it? Or will the hosts start their campaign on a positive note? We shall find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit...

Zimbabwe have defeated the Netherlands in a three-match ODI series played in the Netherlands earlier this year. After some break, the home team will play again in ODI cricket. In this inaugural game, captain Craig Ervine will be hopeful that the team can perform well with both bat and ball and win this one.

The quest to qualify for the World Cup begins. Ten teams but the two will make it. WHO WILL THE TWO BE? Well, still some time before we find out as it is the first day of the qualifiers. The hosts, Zimbabwe, will be taking on Nepal. Have to say the former are firm favourites but Nepal have quality in their side and can well spring a surprise. Let's hope we have a good game on our hands.
